newsitem.title: USA: Safeway reports higher second quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Safeway reports higher second quarter profit.

text.p: Supermarket giant Safeway Inc. Tuesday reported higher fiscal second-quarter profits despite one-time charges for labour disputes and early retirement of debt.

The Pleasanton, Calif-based retailer, which recently acquired supermarket chain Vons Companies Inc., posted net income of $129.9 million, or 52 cents a share, in the three months ended June 14, up from $106.7 million, or 44 cents a share, a year ago. Sales rose to $5.25 billion from $3.95 billion.
Safeway is the second largest food and drug retailer in North America, operating 1,367 stores in the United States and Canada.

The latest quarter included a one-time charge of 2 cents a share for early retirement of debt. Without the charge, safeway's operating results were slightly ahead of Wall Street's consensus prediction of 53 cents a share, according to the First Call service.

Safeway said a 75-day strike in Canada trimmed another 7 cents off the company's second-quarter results. A year ago, a strike in British Columbia and Denver reduced second-quarter profits by about 5 cents a share.

Safeway said the results for the latest quarter included all of the income from Vons, while the year-ago quarter reflected only its 35 percent stake in Vons. On a proforma basis, assuming Safeway had owned all of Vons in both periods, second-quarter proforma sales totalled $5.21 billion a year ago.
Comparable-store sales -- sales in stores open a year -- fell 0.1 percent in the second quarter, largely reflecting the effect of deflation and the timing of the Easter holiday.
Going forward, Safeway and Vons plan to spend more than $800 million in fiscal 1997 to open 40 to 45 new stores and complete more than 180 remodelings.
For the six months ended June 14, Safeway earned $252.4 million, or $1.03 a share, on sales of $9.33 billion, up from $203.1 million, or 85 cents a share, on sales of $7.83 billion.
